# lernapps.net tooling

> Build, check and list learning apps for lernapps.net with an AI assistant. The package @lernapps/tooling is on npm.

## Before you start: check the entry criteria

1. **A shell:** you can run commands, with Node 22.18 or newer, git, and `npm` reaching npmjs.com. If not (a chat in
   the browser, such as chatgpt.com, usually cannot): **stop here and do nothing else.** Tell the creator in two
   sentences that this does not work in this environment and that they should start again in one that does, such as
   the desktop application of their AI assistant, with the same request. Do not build the app by hand from this page.
2. **`npx` may run:** your harness lets you run `npx --yes @lernapps/tooling …` (it runs a package from npm). If its
   permissions block it (an auto mode that refuses code from the internet), tell the creator in two sentences how to
   allow it, e.g. in Claude Code a permission rule `Bash(npx --yes @lernapps/tooling:*)`, and wait. Never work around
   the block. Until it is allowed, start with the fallback below; building the app (Code) needs `npx`.
3. **An empty folder:** the app is the folder you start in. Work in it, never in a subfolder.

## Build an app

1. In the empty folder run `npx --yes @lernapps/tooling init <short name>`. It writes the plan as
   `.vibe/plans/01-<short name>.md`, `AGENTS.md` (the process and every process rule, also below on this page),
   `CLAUDE.md` and the skills of the phases.
2. Read `AGENTS.md`. Then `npx --no -- lernapps plan next` prints the one task to do now, and
   `npx --no -- lernapps plan done` ticks it and prints the next. The plan gives the order, names the skill of each
   task and holds the creator's checkpoints.

Read guidance from the file, in full. Nothing is downloaded: a fetch tool that summarises loses tasks and rules, and
`init` copies the files as they are.

### Fallback: without `npx`, for Explore and Plan

When `npx` may not run yet, the same files come from the repository https://github.com/lernapps/tooling:

1. `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lernapps/tooling` into a temporary folder, not into the app's folder.
2. Copy into the app's folder, unchanged: `guidance/plan-template.md` as `.vibe/plans/01-<short name>.md`,
   `guidance/AGENTS.md` as `AGENTS.md`; write `CLAUDE.md` with the one line `@AGENTS.md`; copy the folders
   `skills/process/*`, `skills/content/*` and `skills/tooling/*` into `.agents/skills/` (each skill a folder with its
   `SKILL.md`).
3. Follow the plan through Explore and Plan, by hand: read it in full, do its tasks in order, tick each box when it
   is done, and set `phase` in its front matter when a phase ends. When the archetype is chosen, also copy
   `skills/archetypes/lernapps-<archetype>-design` into `.agents/skills/`, and put each section of
   `guidance/plan-<archetype>.md` where the plan has the line `<!-- archetype: <name> -->`. Before Code, `npx` must
   run: in the same folder, `npx --yes @lernapps/tooling init <short name>` (the same short name) installs the
   packages and writes the files again; it keeps the plan you filled in. From then on, `lernapps plan` reads and
   ticks the tasks. Without the packages there is no app.

## Change a published app

- In the app's repo, `AGENTS.md` leads to the current plan; `npx --no -- lernapps plan new <short name>` starts the
  plan of the next piece of work.

## Reference

Look things up here when you need them. Not needed for building.

- Rules by id: https://lernapps.net/tooling/rules/ (check messages link `#<id>`).
- Platform rules for an app built without this tooling (by hand, another framework, an app builder):
  node_modules/@lernapps/tooling/skills/tooling/lernapps-cli/references/platform-rules.md (after `npx --yes @lernapps/tooling init`)
- Check a built or published app: `npx --yes @lernapps/tooling check <dir|url>`. Every
  command lists its options with `--help`.
- Schemas: validation report https://lernapps.net/tooling/schemas/validation-report.v1.schema.json, review verdict
  https://lernapps.net/tooling/schemas/verdict.v1.schema.json, catalog entry
  https://lernapps.net/apps/schemas/entry.v1.schema.json. The schemas of a quiz and of an explainer are in the app:
  node_modules/@lernapps/app-templates/runtime/quiz/quiz.v1.schema.json and .../explainer/explainer.v1.schema.json.
- GitHub, explained for creators: https://lernapps.net/tooling/github/
- Keeping an app up to date, the two GitHub Apps and the settings: https://lernapps.net/tooling/github/updates/
- Which assistant to build with, and three apps a budget model built: https://lernapps.net/tooling/assistants/
- How we test the guidance, with eval results: https://lernapps.net/tooling/prompt-engineering/
- Architecture: https://lernapps.net/tooling/architecture/

## Other llms.txt of lernapps.net

- lernapps.net, where to find what: https://lernapps.net/llms.txt

- Catalog: https://lernapps.net/apps/llms.txt; listing an app: https://lernapps.net/apps/enter/llms.txt

The process rules follow below: `AGENTS.md`, the file `init` writes into every app, as it is in this version.

## AGENTS.md

Learning app for lernapps.net: static, runs in the browser, collects nothing, accessible. Built with its creator.

### Before `lernapps init`

No `package.json` with `lernapps.init` here? The app does not exist yet. Ask the creator what they want: an app to
share (topic, grade, what learners do), or to practise for an occasion such as a test. Choose a short name (lower
case, hyphens). Run once, in this folder, `npx --yes @lernapps/tooling init <name>`, or for an occasion
`npx --yes @lernapps/practice init <name>`. It rewrites this file: read it again.

### The plan

- Four phases: Explore, Plan, Code, Commit. The current plan is `.vibe/plans/<NN>-<short name>.md` with the highest
  NN. The creator reads it too.
- `npx --no -- lernapps plan next` prints the one task to do now. Do it, then `npx --no -- lernapps plan done`: it
  ticks the task and prints the next. Does not apply: `plan skip "<reason>"`. More to do: `plan add "<task>"`. A
  task done in part stays open.
- Change tasks, phase and front matter only with `lernapps plan` (`plan-file`). Findings and decisions you write
  into the plan's other sections, in the creator's language.
- A checkpoint: stop, ask, wait. Then `plan done --answer "<the creator's words>"`.
- Every task ticked, more to do: `npx --no -- lernapps plan new <short name>` starts the next plan.
- Begin each reply to the creator with the phase: "**Code**", "**Plan · Checkpoint**".

### Always

- The app is this folder. Every command runs here, never in a subfolder or a copy.
- Load a skill when a task names it. Read each file a task names in full, never summarised.
- Push only the branch the current plan names. A push to `main` publishes.
- Never `--no-verify`.
- Never edit a `lernapps-*` skill: `lernapps update` replaces them. The app's own skills (`app-content`, `app-*`)
  take precedence.
- Nothing about a real learner in any file or commit message (`no-learner-data-in-texts`).
- Learners, teachers, parents: German, plain language. The creator: their language, plain words.

### Process rules

Each rule in full: `@lernapps/tooling/guidance/workflow-rules.md` (in `node_modules/`) and
https://lernapps.net/tooling/rules/.

<!-- process rules: written by scripts/agents-md.ts from guidance/workflow-rules.md -->

| Rule | What | What to do | Lines in workflow-rules.md |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plan-file` | The plan's tasks change only through `lernapps plan` | Change the tasks, the phase and the front matter of a plan only with `lernapps plan`: `next` prints the task to do, `done` ticks it, `skip` ticks a task that does not apply, `add` adds one. Never reword, delete or tick a task by hand. | 7–22 |
| `explore-before-code` | No code before the plan is confirmed | No code and no `lernapps create` until the creator has confirmed the plan with a yes. | 24–32 |
| `stop-at-checkpoints` | Stop at the creator's checkpoints | Checkpoints: research, confirm the plan and the content method, the pattern page (`early-preview`), publish. Stop at each and wait for the answer. | 34–47 |
| `few-turns-after-plan` | Work on your own after the plan | After the confirmation, ask only what you cannot decide; else choose, mark "(guess)" under "Key decisions" and list it in the retrospective. | 49–58 |
| `early-preview` | A pattern page first, with the creator's look | In Code, build one complete page or screen first, check it as a learner would, then show it to the creator and ask whether the other pages may follow it. | 60–71 |
| `feedback-applied-everywhere` | A remark on one page is checked on all | A remark of the creator on one place that is about a pattern, a fact or a term holds for every place: find them all and change them in the same task. | 73–86 |
| `retrospective-filled` | Fill the retrospective | At the end of Commit, fill every part with facts: phases reached, creator turns after the plan, where you guessed. No names. | 88–98 |
| `app-content-guide` | Keep the app's content guide | Keep the app's content guide `.agents/skills/app-content/SKILL.md` complete and true: no placeholder left once content is written, and it says what was built. | 102–120 |
| `app-content-matches` | The content guide says what was built | The guide describes the app as built, so that an agent without your conversation can add the next chapter or round from it alone. | 122–134 |

<!-- end of the process rules -->
